samples.summary: Focus release fires while a slides text-box edit session is still alive (keepalive path), re-arming destructive canvas shortcuts against the element being edited
samples.evidence: The hook is mounted on the whole slides `<Toolbar>` (index.tsx:110), including the `text-edit` contextual section. The docs text-box editor deliberately keeps the edit session mounted when focus moves from the textarea to a control tagged `data-text-edit-keepalive` (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:736-751: "skip the commit so the text-box stays mounted, and the control's own handler re-focuses via api.focus()"). For dropdown-style keepalive controls the re-focus only happens on the *swatch/item-selected* path — `useMenuCloseHandlers` (menu-focus.ts:52-57) explicitly lets Escape / outside-dismiss fall through to Radix's default focus-to-trigger without calling `editor.focus()`. In that state focus sits on the keepalive trigger `<button>`, which is exactly what `isEditableTarget()` (packages/slides/.../interactions/keyboard.ts:882) relied on to suppress the document-level rules. `isReleasable()` has no text-edit guard, so line 104 blurs that button to `document.body`; the slides keydown listener is bound to `document` unconditionally (editor.ts:2727) so with target=body the Delete/Backspace rule (keyboard.ts:215-231) now removes the element the user is still editing, and the printable-key type-to-edit rule (keyboard.ts:663-679) re-enters edit mode with `initialText`. Uncommitted text plus the whole element can be destroyed by one Delete press.

samples.summary: `pointerDriven` is never reset after use and is only cleared by Tab, so stale state lets the hook steal focus from non-pointer / programmatic focus into the toolbar
samples.evidence: `onPointerDown` sets the flag and nothing clears it except `e.key === "Tab"` (line 87) or a later pointerdown outside the toolbar/popup. After any pointer interaction on the toolbar (or in ANY portalled popup anywhere in the app — `POPUP_SELECTOR` at line 35-36 matches every `[role="menu"|"dialog"|"listbox"]`, not just toolbar-owned ones), the next `focusin` inside the toolbar is released, even when that focus was keyboard-driven (arrow/Enter navigation inside an open menu) or programmatic (a re-render / autofocus after `state.kind` flips between idle/object/text-edit). The doc comment at lines 74-78 claims only pointer-driven focus is released; the flag does not implement that invariant.

samples.summary: `setTimeout(..., 0)` fires between pointerdown and click in a real browser, so the blur lands mid-press rather than "once the interaction is finished"
samples.evidence: The release is scheduled from `focusin`, which in a real browser happens on pointerdown; a physical click lasts ~50-150ms, so the 0ms macrotask runs before `pointerup`/`click`. The button therefore loses focus (and any focus-dependent behaviour / focus-visible state) before its own click handler runs — contrary to the module comment (lines 18-19) and unlike the jsdom tests, where userEvent dispatches pointerdown/pointerup/click synchronously so the timer can only fire after the click. Any toolbar control that opens or commits on `click` while reading focus, or that relies on `focus`/`focusout` bookkeeping across the press, sees a different order in production than the suite exercises.

samples.summary: Sibling toolbar driving the same slides editor (BoardToolbar) is not opted in, so issue #882 persists there
samples.evidence: `BoardToolbar` renders `<Toolbar>` at board-toolbar.tsx:178 with no `data-canvas-toolbar` attribute and never calls `useCanvasFocusRelease()`, yet it drives the same `SlidesEditor` whose shortcut rules are gated by `isEditableTarget()` (BUTTON ⇒ skip) on a document-level keydown listener (packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:2727). The same is true of `MobileSlidesToolbar`. The fix is therefore partial: on a board, using any toolbar button still leaves the focused `<button>` as the keydown target and silently disables arrows/Delete/z-order shortcuts.

samples.summary: Outside-click dismissal of a toolbar menu leaves the trigger focused, so the #882 symptom can still be reached
samples.evidence: `onFocusIn` early-returns when `pointerDriven` is false (line 91), and a pointerdown on the canvas sets it false. If any close path returns focus to the toolbar trigger after a pointer-down outside (Radix normally preventDefaults `onCloseAutoFocus` in that case, but controlled menus in this repo override `onCloseAutoFocus` — e.g. menu-focus.ts:52 — and could re-focus the trigger), the release never runs and the focused `<button>` keeps blocking every canvas shortcut. No guard covers the "focus arrived at a toolbar button while the last pointerdown was outside" case.

verdict.reason: Verified independently and end-to-end. (1) The hook is mounted on the whole desktop slides toolbar, whose root carries data-canvas-toolbar and whose contextual slot renders TextEditSection (index.tsx:70,110,136-138). (2) isReleasable() has no text-edit/keepalive exemption — only toolbar-membership, button-ness, and no-open-popup (toolbar-focus-release.ts:55-62), and line 104 blurs to document.body; pointerDriven is cleared only by Tab (line 87), so an Escape dismiss after a pointer-driven open still passes. (3) The docs text-box editor deliberately skips the commit when focus moves to a [data-text-edit-keepalive] control, leaving the session mounted with uncommitted text (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:747-751). (4) On Esc/outside dismiss the text-edit dropdowns intentionally do NOT call editor.focus() and let Radix restore focus to the keepalive trigger <button> (font-family-picker.tsx:147-163 with keepalive trigger at :133; text-paragraph-group.tsx:94-105 with keepalive trigger at :82; menu-focus.ts:52-57 returns early unless a swatch was clicked). (5) That trigger button was the sole suppressor of document-level rules (isEditableTarget returns true for tag === 'BUTTON', keyboard.ts:882). Once blurred to body, the document keydown listener (editor.ts:2727-2729 -> handleKeyDown at 3481-3483, no editing guard) runs the Delete/Backspace rule (keyboard.ts:214-231) against ctx.selection, which enterEditMode set to the element being edited (editor.ts:3970), calling store.removeElements — destroying the element and its uncommitted text; the printable-key rule (keyboard.ts:662-679) likewise re-enters edit mode with initialText. No focus watchdog re-focuses the textarea in either text-box editor. Critical data-loss path in the correctness lane.
